specification.problem: Continuous-time quantum walk spatial search on a small graph with N<=16 vertices, N a power of two, one marked vertex w behind a phase oracle. Compare a single-stage walk at gamma near critical value with a two-stage schedule (gamma1 for T1, then gamma2 for T2). Success is the marked-vertex probability |<w|U|s>|^2.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance, N=8 or 16 vertices on 3 or 4 qubits with no ancillas. A generic walk Hamiltonian H=-gamma*A-|w><w| is simulated by first-order Trotterization with a fixed number of steps. The two-stage schedule applies two successive (gamma,T) pairs. Outside scope: the paper's actual two graph families, their analytic gap and critical gamma values, the exact stage times, and the connectivity-versus-speed scaling analysis.

symbols.meaning: number of vertex qubits, n=log2 N
rates and durations of stage 1 and stage 2
number of Trotter steps per stage

equations.label: Search Hamiltonian
equations.description: Walk Hamiltonian with graph hopping term and oracle term. The abstract only says the walk evolves by Schrödinger's equation, so this form is the standard Childs-Goldstone one.
equations.justification: Standard continuous-time quantum search Hamiltonian. The abstract does not state it.

equations.label: Two-stage evolution
equations.description: Two successive walks with different walking rates. This is the form of a two-stage algorithm in which the walking rate is adjusted.
equations.abstract_quote: a novel two-stage quantum walk algorithm in which the walking rate must be adjusted to yield high search probability
equations.justification: The abstract says the rate is adjusted between two stages. The number of stages is taken as two, with fixed durations.

equations.label: Success probability
equations.description: Probability of reading out the marked vertex from the uniform start state.
equations.justification: Standard figure of merit for spatial search.

equations.label: Trotter step
equations.description: First-order Trotter product. The oracle phase is a controlled phase on |w>, one query per step. For a hypercube, A=sum_j X_j, so e^{i\gamma A t/r}=prod_j RX_j(-2\gamma t/r).
equations.justification: The sketch proposes Trotterization or an exact decomposition. The oracle must be inserted as a placeholder phase gate.
assumptions: Trotter error is small for large r
Oracle phase angle t/r is realised through the black box or a fixed-phase variant
Hypercube factorization applies only if the graph is a hypercube

equations.label: Optimal-time scaling check
equations.latex: T_{opt}(N)=\arg\max_T P(T),\quad T_{opt}\sim c\sqrt{N}\ \text{in the fast case}
equations.description: Scan T (and gamma) at several N and fit T_opt against sqrt(N). This is a claim for the fast-search example, not a verified result.
equations.abstract_quote: searches on $d$-dimensional cubic lattices in $O(\sqrt{N})$ time when $d\geq 5$
equations.justification: O(sqrt N) is the benchmark runtime for fast search, taken here as the target for the low-connectivity fast-search example.
assumptions: N is too small to see asymptotics reliably

registers.name: v
registers.role: vertex index register, little-endian binary encoding of the vertex label, no ancillas

specification.initial_state: Apply H to every qubit of v starting from |0...0> to get |s>.

steps.description: Prepare |s> with Hadamards on all vertex qubits.
Stage 1: run r Trotter steps of the walk at gamma1 for total time T1. Each step applies the graph term, then the oracle phase placeholder.
Stage 2 (two-stage case only): switch to gamma2 and run r Trotter steps for total time T2. Single-stage case sets T2=0.
Classically sweep gamma and T and fit T_opt versus N. Compare with connectivity measures.

specification.measurement: Measure all n vertex qubits in the computational basis. Qiskit is little-endian, so the last character of the counts key is qubit 0, and w must be matched in that order. Estimate P as the frequency of w.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Choose gamma1, gamma2, T1, T2 by grid scan to maximize P. Fit T_opt versus sqrt(N). Compute vertex, edge, algebraic and normalized algebraic connectivity of the graph and compare with speed.
assumptions: N<=16, a power of two, to fit the qubit cap
Marked vertex w is given by a phase oracle black box
Graph A is a small stand-in graph such as a hypercube or a complete-graph pair with a bridge, because the paper's exact graphs are unknown
First-order Trotterization with enough steps stands in for exact evolution
Stage times and rates are numerically scanned, not analytic
